title: geometry (proposed for layout-model/v3.1.0, ADR 0010)
description: The drawing of one interlocking as a design fact: where each named thing sits and how the track runs, in the interlocking's own frame (millimetres from the top-left of its drawn extent, x right, y down). Joined to meaning by name only; never read for connectivity.

polyline.description: Ordered vertices, SVG points syntax: 'x,y x,y ...'. A string because a JSON list is sorted by the canonical form.

placement.description: Where a glyph sits: its origin, its turn (degrees, counter-clockwise as seen on the page, 0/90/180/270) and its mirror (x: top for bottom; y: left for right), applied mirror first. The glyph itself is the reader's.

heads.description: A mast's heads by letter: a head cannot exist alone (view §4).

track.description: One drawn run of track between two things: the circuit it belongs to (absent for dark track) and, where an end is an appliance's track port, that port by name (Sargent:835.R). An end at a joint or a marker is absent: the circuit's bounds are track's business.

marker.description: A track symbol with no railroad name of its own (a joint, END CTC, NextCP, a milepost, a policy sign): its kind as the libraries spell it, its placement, and the circuit at each of its track pins, so a reader joins it to track by name.

circuits.description: The circuit at each track pin of the marker, by pin name; a pin on dark track is absent.

mileposts.description: Milepost anchors by milepost (ADR 0004 D7: the Value is the milepost, so it is the marker's name). Luchessa draws two; Sargent none.
